messages:
maria: Heads up — infra alert from perf-bot: p99 generation latency up ~12% on multi-GPU stacks since yesterday 00:30 UTC. :eyes:
devperf-bot: perf-alert: model=gpt-neox-20B, topology=tp2-pp1 (2-way tensor, no pipeline), batch=4, devices=8, p99_baseline=180ms current=201ms, correlation with NCCL env toggles suspected
lee: saw this on staging too. timeline matches the kernel selector change we rolled out (kv-prefetch heuristic + new kernel family fallback).
anjali: any profiling traces? nvprof/nsys snapshots?
maria: i grabbed an nsys trace and a few NCCL perf logs. attaching quick snippet: ```ncu --target-processes all -o trace ./infer.sh --bench``` main findings: allreduce stalls increase by ~2.8ms/iter, KV cache hit pattern shows more uneven sequence lengths -> batching skew
ryan: guessing algo/proto mismatch causing extra communication rounds. last good config used NCCL_PROTO=LL but the runtime suggested LL128 for larger tokens.
sara: ll128 normally helps bandwidth but can cause higher kernel launch overhead for small collectives. our sequence length distribution has 10% long tails now (due to prompt mixing).
lee: can we repro with a controlled workload? create two runs: (1) all-LL, (2) LL128 + default algo, (3) LL128 + RING, (4) LL128 + TREE. measure per-step allreduce time.
maria: I ran a quick sweep: ```export NCCL_PROTO=LL128; export NCCL_ALGO=RING; ./bin/infer --batch=4 --seqdist=mix_long_tail``` results: allreduce_mean=3.9ms, wait_mean=2.6ms, p99_latency=215ms
anjali: same workload with LL: allreduce_mean=1.6ms, wait_mean=0.9ms, p99_latency=188ms — so LL is better here. Suggests LL128 kernel startup cost dominates for our small collectives.
ryan: interesting — kernel selector might be choosing LL128 because of wrong cost model estimating bandwidth wins. kernel selector inputs: seq_len_mean, kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_kv_prefetch. need to add a penalty term for small-reduce counts.
sara: also noticed channel usage shifted from 8->4 after kernel change. fewer channels + LL128 seems to increase head-of-line blocking.
maria: proposed experiment: force channels=8 + LL128, and another with ALGO=RING vs TREE. quick env: ```NCCL_MAX_NRINGS=8 NCCL_PROTO=LL128 NCCL_ALGO=RING ./run```
lee: FYI NCCL envs vary by version. on 2.14 we saw different defaults. include NCCL_DEBUG=INFO to get per-channel throughput logs.
anjali: will add a lightweight micro-benchmark to runtime test harness: synthetic KV patterns (uniform vs long-tail) + small collective sizes to estimate break-even points.
ryan: also add a check in kernel selector to prefer LL for collective_count < 32 and fallback to LL128 only when message_size > 64KB or rings_available>4.
maria: can someone file a perf regression PR with telemetry? include the nsys trace, NCCL logs, and the micro-bench results. mark as P1 for next iteration.
sara: quick patch posted: link-to-pr (WIP) — adds a heuristic: "prefer_ll_for_small_collectives": true and toggles channel_count tuning.
lee: can we A/B route 10% of traffic on dedicated pool to the new selector vs baseline? use rollout canary in console.
anjali: yes — will prepare canary config: 10% traffic, sampling enabled, detailed traces for any p99 exceedance.
maria: thanks team. action items: anjali -> add microbench + canary, ryan -> kernel selector change, sara -> PR and test matrix, lee -> launch canary, maria -> gather traces & update incident.
ryan: one more note: once KV cache skew reduces (we have a fix in next landing), LL128 might become net positive. keep selector adaptive and flag-driven. :thumbsup:
